newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks soar at close on jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks soar at close on jobs data.

text.p: A sharp fall in unemployment figures realesed in late trade kept the bulls charging right up to the final bell in Mexican stock trading on Wednesday, traders said.
"Unemployment figures boosted stocks, and the other fundamental reason was down to the plunge in Cetes rates," a floor trader said.
Final closing figures showed the leading IPC share index had gained 70.15 points, or 1.85 percent, at 3,867.20.
Trading volume had gained from an anemic start to total a brisk 113.01 million shares by the close of trade, by which time traders said they were "snowed under" with buy orders.
Mexico's National Statistics Institute announced open unemployment for February was 4.2 percent, considerably down on year-ago figures of 6.3 percent.
Dealers said that unlike developed markets, falling unemployment is not seen in Mexico as a harbinger of interest rate hikes, but rather as a welcome sign of recovery from a painful economic crisis.
Dealers said Telmex L shares, and shares listed by holding company Grupo Carso and telecom Carso Global Telecom bolstered the market.
All three have corporate links and together accounted for 48 percent of all shares traded during the session.
"Telmex took a flying leap and that pulled up the bourse. Demand was heavy and dealers switched between Telmex, Gcarso and Telecom," a floor trader said.
Gcarso gained 65 centavos to 45.90 pesos, while Telecom also climbed 65 centavos to close at 24.40 pesos.
Telmex ADRs meanwhile shrugged off a downdraft on Wall Street to soar 1-1/8 to a year high of 41-5/8. Telmex also traded heavily in New York, where it ended fifth from the top in volume terms.
Telmex ended at an all-time record close in peso terms of 16.58 pesos, 48 centavos up on the day and just shy of an intraday high of 16.60 pesos.
The Dow Jones ended off 0.27 percent at 6,877.68 points.
A technical analyst noted the IPC cracked resistance during today's session.
"Today the bourse broke resistance at 3,850 points and could head for 3,950 points," said Jaime Fernndez, a technical analyst at the Interacciones brokerage in Mexico City.
"But we think it would get no further, as there was much quick in-and-out dealing," he added.
Fundamental analysts said a favorable outlook for inflation and less pressure from the Mexico drug certification issue kick-started the rally.

"Inflation figures for the first half of March are due out next Monday, and we expect them to be down, and the certification row has calmed down," said Esteban Rojas, deputy head of research at the Arka brokerage in Mexico City. Nonetheless, Fernndez urged caution on the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on March 25.
"We believe they will indeed raise U.S. rates, which the market has not discounted. That could hit it later on," he said.
On the broad market, 107 stocks changed hands, of which 58 gained while 31 declined.
Financial groups Banacci and GFB were among the prominent gainers in the wake of sharp falls in interest rates, tarders said.
Banacci climbed 16 centavos to 18.96 pesos, while GFB gained 10 centavos to 3.00 pesos.
The other member of Mexico's "big three" financial groups, Serfin, did not share its counterparts' fortunes and closed down 20 centavos at 3.20 peso.
Traders noted ING Barings cut Serfin from buy to sell in early trade, following a flurry of mixed news concerning the stock.
((-- Karina Balderas, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9562))
